item.title: Sunscreen for lakes and dams: Could a thin floating layer of nanomaterial shield water from evaporation?
item.description: Water stored in dams and reservoirs for humans to use often evaporates, especially in hot regions like southern Africa. Rising temperatures speed up evaporation, leaving less water for people, farming and industry. Daniel Kwasi Kpeglo has just completed a Ph.D. in physics. He explains his laboratory research into a new design—a thin nanomaterial floating cover that could be placed over lakes and dams like a blanket, reducing evaporation by limiting the amount of infrared heat from the sun that reaches the water. He also outlines what hurdles need to be cleared for the design to be tested in… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why banks in Ghana make little use of AI for climate action decisions

The study is published in Discover Sustainability. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Congo Basin study reveals nuanced relationship between people and flooding
item.description: In the Lac Télé Community Reserve, a vast tropical peatland in Africa's Congo Basin that is home to about 20,000 people, the forces of climate change and globalization are hitting residents hard. The seasonal floods upon which village communities have long relied are arriving earlier, staying longer and pushing farther into places that used to remain dry. And these impacts vary dramatically from one village to the next, a new Yale-led study finds. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 14 fossilised teeth from Egypt reveal five extinct ancient shark species
item.description: Fossilised shark teeth from Egypt's Western Desert reveal prehistoric ocean life. Scientists discovered teeth from five extinct shark species in the Abu-Tartur Plateau region. This discovery highlights Egypt's ancient marine environments hidden beneath its deserts. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Mawlid festivities cancelled in Ethiopia's Tigray region over fears of drone strikes
item.description: In Ethiopia, festivities marking Mawlid, the Muslim holiday celebrating the birth of the Prophet Mohammed, have been cancelled at the last minute over fears of drone strikes. The cancellation comes just days after another major Tigrayan festival, Ashenda, was also called off at the last minute for the same reason. Drone strikes hit northern Ethiopia in recent days, as tensions between the Tigray People’s Liberation Front and the Ethiopian government continue to escalate. FRANCE 24's Tom Canetti reports from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Fuente: France 24 - English.
